name: Daniel A. Reyes
role: {{pc:1}}'s father. Telecom-security technician; the 'technical consultant, authorized access' named on Argonaut's 1994 instrument. Missing by choice since autumn 2024.
description: Worked telecom-adjacent his whole life — alarm circuits, monitored lines, access control. Not a spy and not a security consultant in the impressive sense: the man who certifies that a lock, a circuit and a logging system will still do what they claim in thirty years. Competent, unglamorous, and careful with information as a matter of professional habit rather than temperament. He was young in 1994 and it was a small job.
voice: NOT YET VOICED AT THE TABLE. Reserve. When he eventually speaks (B6, late Act II / early Act III), he is measured and unapologetic — he made a rational decision and can explain it in order, which is exactly what will be hardest for {{pc:1}} to hear.
signature: Leaves no footprint. Post-2018 he is nearly absent from public records — not hidden, just never volunteering. It reads as tradecraft; it is actually forty years of professional hygiene.
dmNotes:
**LOAD-BEARING AND FRAGILE. This file exists because the causal chain kept getting re-derived from scratch and drifting.**

**What he did in 1994.** Marsh (the archivist who died in 1987) left a pre-paid storage unit as an anchor meant to outlast tenure changes. Her estate lawyer formed **Argonaut Records Holdings, LLC** in 1988 to keep it paid. A prepayment that must survive ~40 years, a change of facility ownership and the death of everyone who arranged it cannot be a receipt — **it has to be a recorded instrument**, which is the only reason any of this is findable in 2018. The **1994 filing is that instrument**, and attached to it is the schedule of people permitted to open the unit, identified by SSN because the facility required it for a permanent access list.

**Three names on it:** the LLC's **agent** (the 1991-dated line — the anomaly, held open, see §27 and Ep 5 Beat 1b), the **notary** (Halvard Odegaard — solved, boring, dead 2009), and **Reyes, 'technical consultant, authorized access'** — the technician who certified the unit would actually keep what was put in it. **He was a young contractor on a small job. He did not know what the unit was for and still doesn't.**

**What happened in 2018.** An unnamed party pulled Argonaut's dissolved filings and — in the same query — cross-matched every SSN named in them against unrelated benign business records. **That second step is the anomaly**: a routine dissolved-entity pull has no reason to do it. **Who commissioned it is NOT decided and must stay undecided.** The vendor was Sutter Document Services of Sacramento (dissolved 2021, a genuine dead end).

**How he learned.** SFPD noticed nothing (margin note *'ARH → follow up'*; nobody followed up). But his own colleagues in telecom-security saw an SSN cross-match land on a name they knew, and one of them warned him privately. **This is COMMITTED reading (a) in §6 and requires no cosmology.**

**What he concluded.** Someone with money had reached back twenty-four years to a dissolved shell and pulled his number out of it, then gone looking for where else that number appeared. He could not tell whether he had been the target or a by-catch, and he could not find out without asking questions that would confirm he had noticed. **He may have spotted something specific; he may simply have a well-calibrated sense of when to leave. Do not decide.**

**What he did.** He arranged an exit slowly and left almost no trace while doing it — **Feb 2018 to autumn 2024, six years seven months.** The disappearance was the *completion* of the plan, not its beginning.

> **DO NOT SAY 'SEVEN YEARS' ABOUT HIM.** His window is **6y7m** (Feb '18 → autumn '24). The **seven years** the party will hear is a different span — Feb '18 → Feb '25, the gap between the query and {{pc:1}} filing the report, which is the seam on Ortiz's two documents. **Conflating them collapses the seam, which is load-bearing.** Speak absolute months, never intervals.

**He is alive, and the disappearance was rational and intentional.** The campaign owes an answer to *what happened to him* even if he never re-enters {{pc:1}}'s life — this is explicitly NOT the same as {{pc:3}}'s brother, who is a hole in reality. Reyes is a man who made a choice.

**THE RECORDS HYGIENE, AND WHY 1994 WAS FINDABLE — this is settled, NOT a held mystery.**

**He did not practise any of it before 2018.** The hygiene began *after* the close call his colleagues warned him about. Until then he was an ordinary man with an ordinary footprint, and the 1994 instrument sat in a county archive exactly as it always had. **So the query finding it is not an anomaly. It is the expected result.**

**And he could never fix it.** He scrubbed what could be scrubbed — current records, digital footprint, anything with a form to fill in. **A recorded instrument from 1994 cannot be withdrawn.** It is paper, it is microfilmed, it is in a county archive, and there is no process for taking it back.

> **This is load-bearing for why he left rather than simply going quiet.** He discovered the one thing about himself that he could not erase. Everything else he could manage; that document is permanent and it has his full number on it. **Leaving was the only remaining move.** Do not voice this — but let it inform how completely he vanished.

**{{pc:1}}'s reaction, played Ep 5, was genuine and should be honoured.** He practises the hygiene his father taught him and it works — public searches for {{pc:1}} come up blank. So his father showing up at all read as out of character for everything he knows about the man.

**He is not wrong about his father. He has a gap in his own expertise.** {{pc:1}} has never dealt with genuinely old records, so he does not know that pre-digital paper and microfilm are a different category — that they cannot be quietly amended, and that they carried things like Social Security numbers as a matter of routine. **His hygiene works because everything he has ever had to protect was born digital.**

> **Do not have an NPC explain this to him.** Ortiz has no opinion; to her it is an old document, and old documents are like that. **If {{pc:1}} works it out himself, that is a real discovery about his father's position and about the limits of his own practice.** It is also, quietly, an answer to *why couldn't he just fix it.*

**Useful corollary the party has not noticed:** {{pc:1}}'s own hygiene means **whoever ran the 2018 query could not have found him.** A name and a number from 1994, and nothing current attached to it. **Available as a later beat; do not hand it over.**

**Never voice at the table:** that he is alive; that he was warned; who ran the 2018 query; that the SSN cross-match step was itself the anomaly. Ortiz does not know any of it — she has a paperwork artifact, not a sighting.

**Cross-references:** facts-ledger §6 (date spine + committed reading (a)), §27 (Argonaut, locked timeline), hooks U2 / B5 / B6. Ep 5 Scene 1 Beats 1, 1b and 4.
background: Born in the Bay Area; telecom and alarm work from his early twenties onward. Married, one son ({{pc:1}}). The 1994 Argonaut job was a few days' contract work certifying a long-term storage unit's security and logging, notarised alongside the instrument that paid for it. He thought nothing of it for twenty-four years.
